page.text:
The whole of the mathematics developed in these pages is built from a
single kind of object -- the *set* -- and a single primitive relation
between sets -- *membership*. Numbers, ordered pairs, functions, and the
algebraic structures of later chapters are all, in the end, particular
sets. This chapter fixes the rules that sets obey, in the form of the
axioms of Zermelo and Fraenkel, and then uses those rules to construct
the first sets we need.
